source.question: e-493
source.value:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot (2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(2{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{(e)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-2{(1)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})]-6{\int }_{1}^{e}x\text{d}x \\  & =6{e}^{2}-6(\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3{x}^{2}{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3({e}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

source.question: e-3993
source.value:
At first, it may not look like we have two factors. Actually, we do, but one of them is implicit. The trick is to write the integral as

$$
\int \ln{x}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln{x} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x.
$$

 

Using this trick, we can now use integration by parts. We let

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the by-parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
